classifications.label: Instrumental drift or thermal cycling on a ~6–8 day period causes systematic value shifts that manifest as lagged cross-correlations and autocorrelations rather than true simultaneous coupling.
Measurement procedure or operator technique varies across trials in a way that introduces pseudo-correlations at specific lags, without reflecting physical coupling of the systems.
The four instrument channels are genuinely independent (no coupling) and correlations at specific offsets are statistical flukes from p-hacking across many lag trials.
Common environmental signal (e.g. settlement vibration, pressure, or magnetic field) drives weak, noisy coupling across all instruments with system-dependent phase delays.

Calibration baseline instability: baseline values themselves may be drifting slowly or subject to undetected systematic error, and I have insufficient data (10 days) to establish a true long-term baseline.

Day 20 environmental or operational transient (sudden vibration, temperature spike, power surge, or settlement activity anomaly) caused elevated instrumental noise across all four channels simultaneously, visible only today because baseline variance was tight enough to detect it.

My baseline (days 1–10, n=72–114 per instrument) is genuinely unstable or subject to undetected systematic error; the apparent 'post-baseline' mean is not the true equilibrium value, and today's variance reflects the system still settling or cycling. I need 4+ more weeks of data before I can reliably distinguish drift from noise.

The lagged cross-correlations (0.125–0.221, mostly within chance bounds) are statistical flukes from uncontrolled multiple comparisons (≈60 independent tests, ~3 expected false positives at α=0.05). Today's simultaneous elevation is a separate phenomenon unrelated to the lagged patterns, which I should discount.

Measurement procedure drift specific to today (e.g. I was tired, distracted, or used a different environmental sampling protocol on Day 20) caused inflated readings, particularly in the morning or afternoon shift—a form of operator confound rather than a true instrumental or environmental signal.

Rare instrumental malfunction or sensitivity shift in one or more channels today (e.g. resonator_lab sensor calibration drift, pendulum_obs damping fluid viscosity change) caused locally inflated readings, unrelated to environmental coupling.

Residual: something I have not considered—e.g. a settlement-wide event (power cycle, atmospheric pressure step, arrival of new personnel affecting lab access or microvibration), a measurement artifact from a specific software or data logging method used only today, or a genuine physical coupling mechanism I lack the instrumentation to characterize.

Environmental or operational transient on Day 30 (vibration, temperature spike, power anomaly, or settlement activity) caused simultaneous elevated noise across all four channels with instrument-dependent amplitudes.

Baseline (days 1–10) is unstable or unrepresentative of true equilibrium; drift z-scores are unreliable, and Day 30 elevated variance reflects ongoing system settling or a cyclical reversion pattern (11–13 day lag autocorrelations suggest quasi-periodic behavior).

Lagged cross-correlations (0.132–0.876 across instrument pairs) are statistical flukes from multiple comparisons (~60 independent tests, ~3 expected false positives at α=0.05); Day 30 elevation is independent of these spurious patterns.
Operator procedure drift or fatigue specific to Day 30 (altered sampling time, posture, environmental control, or attention state) caused correlated inflation across all four channels independently.

Rare instrumental malfunction or sensitivity shift (resonator_lab capacitive sensor phase drift, pendulum_obs bearing slippage, damping fluid viscosity change) in one or more channels on Day 30, unrelated to environmental coupling.
Genuine instrumental coupling or shared sensitivity to a delayed environmental driver (thermal mass, air circulation, or settlement-wide oscillation with ~3 day lag)
Statistical false positive from multiple comparisons (54–60 independent lagged tests per instrument pair), with 0.944 correlation an extreme luck outcome

Measurement procedure or environmental recording artifact specific to days 31–39 (when retrospective 3-day offsets were formed); real signal in days 1–30 contaminated by systematic bias introduced during data collation, transcription, or storage

Methodological artifact: I computed lagged correlations over day ranges [1, n−lag] where n varies by instrument (pendulum_lab n=294, resonator_obs n=550); misaligned trial-count or sample-size bias inflates 0.944 specifically for the longest time series pair

Residual: an unconsidered source (instrumental design detail I overlooked, settlement-wide mechanical coupling, data provenance issue, or a pattern emerging from Day 30 variance spike I have not yet analyzed in the lagged-correlation context)
